items.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I mean Coltrane and Charlie Parker and Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: No, there seems to be a lot of press about — books about, what about the white guys’ contribution to jazz these days, and there’s some stuff floating around, and I just wondered if it got down—

No I don’t see it. I mean I’ve read stuff like that, and I feel there’s bitter people in any kind of race, any place on the planet. And if that’s what they want to do, great. I mean you certainly can’t take away from what black artists have done, and they certainly have been leaders, I mean Coltrane and Charlie Parker and Louis Armstrong. You know, but then we’ve had Bill Evans and I mean music is music and art is art, and it’s personal preference to me. I have people I love that are black and white and yellow…
San Diego is quite the ethnic — a variety of ethnic—
